I am 72 years old. I finished primary school and then worked outside, but I have been farming my own land here in Quzhou County for 20 years now. It is just me and my wife at home — two people — and we have a well for irrigation. My farm is a bit over 10 mu, and everyone around here does wheat in winter and maize in summer, so that is what I do too. I do not try new tricks. I watch what my neighbors do, especially Lao Wang across the road, and I do what I did last year unless something went wrong.

For the winter wheat, I will rotary till the ground before sowing. I sow about 30 jin of improved wheat seed per mu — I buy the same kind Lao Wang used because his crop stood well last year. At sowing time, I put down half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu, that is 25 kg. Then in March when the wheat turns green, I spread another 30 kg of urea per mu on top. The dealer told me once that 20 kg is enough, but I would rather put a bit too much than see my wheat turn yellow. A bag of urea is over 100 yuan now, and five bags of compound fertilizer is another big cost, but losing yield is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just money out of pocket. I irrigate three times: once before winter to help it survive, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray four times in total: herbicide once in early spring, insecticide twice for aphids, and fungicide once because there was rust going around two years ago. I hire a machine to spray now because my back cannot carry the tank anymore. I expect about 1000 jin per mu if the weather is normal.

For the summer maize, I plant right after the wheat harvest in June. There is no time to plough, and the neighbors all use no-tillage now, so I hire the no-till seeder too. I use hybrid seed — about 3 jin per mu, which is one and a half of those small packages. I put 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the row at planting, and then when the maize gets to the big trumpet stage, I spread 35 kg of urea per mu. That is a lot of urea, but I want the ears big and full. I irrigate twice: once right after planting if the soil is dry, and once when the tassels come out. I spray three times: herbicide once, and insecticide twice for corn borer. I expect about 1200 jin per mu. All of this — seed, fertilizer, hired spraying, hired planting — costs me over 5000 yuan for the year. I have to balance it carefully. If I spend too much on fertilizer, I have less cash for hiring help, but at my age I must hire someone for the heavy work.
